sources.title: AI Agents for Scientific Literature Research
sources.snippet: How should a multi-agent system conduct a scientific literature review while preserving citation fidelity, uncertainty, and methodological nuance? Scientific research agents need source-aware division of labor, claim-level provenance, method-quality assessment, and explicit handling of contradictory findings.

sources.title: Autonomous Data Analysis Agents
sources.snippet: How should agents combine code execution, data profiling, statistical checks, visualization, and narrative synthesis in a trustworthy analysis workflow? The strongest design separates hypothesis generation from executable analysis and requires the narrative agent to cite computed artifacts rather than infer results from natural-language guesses.

sources.title: Benchmarks and Metrics for Evaluating AI Agents
sources.snippet: Which metrics best capture agent quality beyond final-answer accuracy, especially for long-horizon and multi-agent workflows? A credible evaluation should combine task success with process measures such as tool correctness, citation fidelity, recovery, cost, latency, policy compliance, and reproducibility.

sources.title: Cascading Hallucinations in Multi-Agent Pipelines
sources.snippet: Why can multi-agent chains amplify fabricated facts, and which architectural controls reduce error propagation? Multi-agent composition can turn an early unsupported claim into shared context and apparent consensus; provenance tracking and mandatory re-verification at handoffs are key mitigations.

sources.title: Centralized Orchestrators vs Decentralized Agent Coordination
sources.snippet: What are the trade-offs between a central supervisor agent and decentralized peer-to-peer coordination for long research workflows? Central orchestration simplifies global state and accountability, while decentralized designs can improve resilience and parallelism but require stronger protocols for consensus and conflict handling.
